claims.title: The Baptism of Poland
claims.summary: Duke Mieszko I accepted Christianity in the Latin rite, conventionally dated to 14 April 966, bringing his realm into Western Christendom and marking the traditional birth of the Polish state.

sources.label: Historical Facts about the Baptism of Poland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-966-the-baptism-of-poland, claim TL:POL:event:966:the-baptism-of-poland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Congress of Gniezno
claims.summary: Emperor Otto III made pilgrimage to Gniezno and an independent Polish church province was established, recognising the young state's standing within Christian Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1000-congress-of-gniezno, claim TL:POL:event:1000:congress-of-gniezno, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coronation of Boleslaw I the Brave
claims.summary: Boleslaw I was crowned king at Gniezno, the first ruler to bear the royal title of Poland and to win recognition of the realm as a kingdom rather than a duchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1025-coronation-of-boleslaw-i-the-brave, claim TL:POL:event:1025:coronation-of-boleslaw-i-the-brave, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Testament of Boleslaw III and fragmentation
claims.summary: The dying Boleslaw III Wrymouth divided Poland among his sons, beginning nearly two centuries of fragmentation into rival duchies that weakened the state against its neighbours.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1138-testament-of-boleslaw-iii-and-fragmentation, claim TL:POL:event:1138:testament-of-boleslaw-iii-and-fragmentation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Casimir III the Great
claims.summary: The last Piast king reformed the law, founded the University of Krakow in 1364, expanded the kingdom and welcomed Jewish settlers, leaving Poland prosperous and consolidated.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1333-reign-of-casimir-iii-the-great, claim TL:POL:event:1333:reign-of-casimir-iii-the-great, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Krewo and the Jagiellonian dynasty
claims.summary: The agreement at Krewo arranged the marriage of Queen Jadwiga to Jogaila of Lithuania, who was baptised as Wladyslaw II Jagiello, joining Poland and Lithuania under a new dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1385-union-of-krewo-and-the-jagiellonian-dynasty, claim TL:POL:event:1385:union-of-krewo-and-the-jagiellonian-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Grunwald
claims.summary: Polish and Lithuanian forces under Wladyslaw II Jagiello destroyed the army of the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald, halting the Order's eastward expansion in the Baltic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1410-battle-of-grunwald, claim TL:POL:event:1410:battle-of-grunwald, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Copernicus publishes 'On the Revolutions'
claims.summary: The Polish astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus published his heliocentric theory, placing the Sun rather than the Earth at the centre of the cosmos and helping to launch modern astronomy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1543-copernicus-publishes-on-the-revolutions, claim TL:POL:event:1543:copernicus-publishes-on-the-revolutions, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Lublin
claims.summary: Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania united into a single federal state, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, ruled by an elected monarch and a common Sejm, one of Europe's largest powers.

sources.label: The Act of the Union of Lublin document

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1569-union-of-lublin, claim TL:POL:event:1569:union-of-lublin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Relief of Vienna
claims.summary: King John III Sobieski led the allied cavalry charge that broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna, marking the high point of the Commonwealth's military reputation in Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1683-relief-of-vienna, claim TL:POL:event:1683:relief-of-vienna, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Deluge
claims.summary: A devastating Swedish invasion during the Second Northern War ravaged the Commonwealth, causing enormous loss of life and population and accelerating the state's long decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1655-the-deluge, claim TL:POL:event:1655:the-deluge, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Partitions of Poland
claims.summary: In three stages (1772, 1793, 1795) Russia, Prussia and Austria divided the Commonwealth among themselves, despite the reforming Constitution of 3 May 1791, ending Polish statehood for 123 years.

sources.label: Constitution of 3 May 1791
sources.publisher: Polish History Museum / Google Arts & Culture

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1772-the-partitions-of-poland, claim TL:POL:event:1772:the-partitions-of-poland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Congress of Vienna and the 'Congress Kingdom'
claims.summary: The post-Napoleonic settlement re-divided the Polish lands and created a nominally autonomous Kingdom of Poland under the Russian tsar, entrenching foreign rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1815-congress-of-vienna-and-the-congress-kingdom, claim TL:POL:event:1815:congress-of-vienna-and-the-congress-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The November Uprising
claims.summary: Poles in the Russian partition rose against the tsar; after initial successes the rising was crushed, bringing reprisals, the end of the Kingdom's autonomy and a wave of political exile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1830-the-november-uprising, claim TL:POL:event:1830:the-november-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The January Uprising
claims.summary: A protracted guerrilla insurrection against Russian rule ended in defeat and severe repression, including executions, deportations to Siberia and intensified Russification.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1863-the-january-uprising, claim TL:POL:event:1863:the-january-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Restoration of independence
claims.summary: As the partitioning empires collapsed at the end of the First World War, an independent Polish state was proclaimed under Jozef Pilsudski, ending 123 years without statehood.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1918-restoration-of-independence, claim TL:POL:event:1918:restoration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Warsaw
claims.summary: Polish forces under Pilsudski halted the advance of the Soviet Red Army outside Warsaw, securing the independence of the young republic in the Polish-Soviet War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1920-battle-of-warsaw, claim TL:POL:event:1920:battle-of-warsaw, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German and Soviet invasion of Poland
claims.summary: Nazi Germany invaded on 1 September, starting the Second World War in Europe; the Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September, and the two powers again partitioned Poland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1939-german-and-soviet-invasion-of-poland, claim TL:POL:event:1939:german-and-soviet-invasion-of-poland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau and the Holocaust on Polish soil
claims.summary: Germany operated its largest concentration and extermination camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau, where some 1.1 million people, overwhelmingly Jews, were murdered as part of the genocide carried out across occupied Poland.

sources.label: Auschwitz Birkenau German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp (1940-1945)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1940-auschwitz-birkenau-and-the-holocaust-on-polish, claim TL:POL:event:1940:auschwitz-birkenau-and-the-holocaust-on-polish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Warsaw Uprising
claims.summary: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupiers in Warsaw; after 63 days the rising was crushed, much of the city was destroyed and tens of thousands of civilians were killed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1944-the-warsaw-uprising, claim TL:POL:event:1944:the-warsaw-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Establishment of communist rule
claims.summary: Backed by the Soviet Union and rigged elections, a communist government consolidated power, founding the Polish People's Republic within the Soviet bloc.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1947-establishment-of-communist-rule, claim TL:POL:event:1947:establishment-of-communist-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of Solidarity
claims.summary: Strikes at the Gdansk shipyard led by Lech Walesa produced Solidarity, the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc, which rapidly grew to about ten million members.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1980-birth-of-solidarity, claim TL:POL:event:1980:birth-of-solidarity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Martial law
claims.summary: The communist authorities imposed martial law, banned Solidarity and interned its leaders, including Walesa, driving the movement underground for the rest of the decade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1981-martial-law, claim TL:POL:event:1981:martial-law, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Semi-free elections and the fall of communism
claims.summary: Round Table talks produced partly free elections that Solidarity won overwhelmingly, ending communist rule in Poland and helping trigger the collapse of the Soviet bloc.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-1989-semi-free-elections-and-the-fall-of-communism, claim TL:POL:event:1989:semi-free-elections-and-the-fall-of-communism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: Poland joined the European Union, completing its return to the West after the fall of communism and accelerating its economic and political integration into Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Poland: A thousand years between the great powers, surviving partition and conquest to rise again.", terralore.co/country/POL/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:POL:event:2004:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
